sentences.text: The name Nodocephalosaurus translates to "knob-headed lizard," a reference to the bulbous osteoderms fused to the top of its skull.
Sullivan originally diagnosed the animal by these bulbous skull features, a prominent quadratojugal horn, and a distinct post-maxillary and lacrimal osteoderm.
The squamosal horns arch backward and end in a rounded point.
Scientists estimated this creature to be 4.5 meters long and weigh 1.5 tonnes.
The only known specimen of Nodocephalosaurus is a partial skull.
A partial skull of Nodocephalosaurus was discovered in 1995 in the De-na-zin member of the Kirtland Formation in New Mexico.
Robert M. Sullivan named Nodocephalosaurus in 1999.
The holotype specimen of Nodocephalosaurus is housed at the State Museum of Pennsylvania in Harrisburg.
In 2000, Tracy Ford assigned a single pup-tent scute (NMMNH P-20880), a type of dermal scale, to Nodocephalosaurus.
Six fossil occurrences of this genus have been recorded.
The presence of Nodocephalosaurus indicates that ankylosaurids were more diverse than nodosaurids in the San Juan Basin.
Contemporary non-dinosaur species included a choristodere, crocodylomorphs like Denazinosuchus, several turtles, and fish such as Melvius and Myledaphus.
It is a member of the class Ornithischia.
The animal is classified within the family Ankylosauridae.
It belongs to the subfamily Ankylosaurinae.
Vickaryous et al. (2004) interpreted Nodocephalosaurus as Ankylosauridae incertae sedis, meaning its exact position within the family was uncertain.
The animal lived between 73.49 and 73.04 million years ago during the late Campanian to early Maastrichtian stages.
The genus existed from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
It inhabited a floodplain on the western edge of the Western Interior Seaway rich in ferns, conifers, and flowering plants.
Evidence suggests the environment had a warm temperate to subtropical climate.
Arbour and Currie (2015) assigned most referred Nodocephalosaurus specimens to Ankylosauridae indet. after discovering other ankylosaurids in the same formation.
